turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on my son's essay, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Save it for the email you'll be sending me. Who decided on the zero?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
Write your own email, Hale. I'm here about Owen, and I have until 4:40. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
Flattery won't get you out of this. Either you explain the zero or I'm going to the principal's office with it.
